title: AI Search, D1 - AI Search supports D1 databases as a data source (beta)
summary:
AI Search can now use a D1 database as a data source. AI Search runs a read-only query that you provide and indexes each returned row as a separate document. Scheduled syncs keep the index current as rows are added, changed, or removed.

Create D1-backed instances from the dashboard, the REST API, or the Workers binding.

title: AI Search - Manage AI Search instances in any namespace with Terraform
summary:
Starting with Cloudflare Terraform provider ↗︎ v5.29.0, you can manage AI Search instances in any namespace, not only default.

The cloudflare_ai_search_instance resource has a new namespace argument. It defaults to default, so existing configurations keep managing the same instances.

title: AI Search - AI Search can generate file summaries during indexing
summary:
AI Search can now summarize your files while it indexes them. For each text document that produces at least three chunks, AI Search uses a large language model (LLM) to generate a summary, topics, and keywords:

  • The summary and keywords are stored in the item's context metadata. A context value you already set is kept.
  • The topics are added to the context header of the file's chunks to help retrieval.

Turn on file summaries in the dashboard, or set indexing_options.file_summary to true when you create or update an instance. File summaries are off by default, and changing the setting triggers a full reindex.

indexing_options is replaced as a whole on every update. Include the current value of every option, or the options you leave out return to their defaults.

The LLM costs are billed to your account. File summaries are not part of the AI Search ingestion allotment. AI Search uses a Workers AI model suited to summarization and calls it through your instance's AI Gateway, or the default gateway if none is set, and the calls are billed as Workers AI usage. Each new or modified file is summarized once, so costs grow with the amount of content you index.

For more information, refer to File summaries.

title: AI Search - Introducing Search for Agents
summary:
Search for Agents makes your website searchable by AI agents without manually configuring a search integration. Turn it on under Quick Actions on your domain's Overview page in the Cloudflare dashboard. Cloudflare creates an AI Search instance, starts indexing your content, and exposes a search endpoint on your domain.

Cloudflare adds discovery metadata to your HTML pages and, when Markdown for Agents is on, to Markdown responses. Agents can discover the endpoint and search with keywords or natural-language queries:

The endpoint supports both GET and HTTP QUERY requests. It returns relevant content in Markdown, not an AI-generated answer, so agents can use the results with their own models.

Search for Agents is available on all plans. Usage is subject to AI Search pricing and plan limits. You can customize configurable settings in the AI Search instance created for your domain.
